clue.text: Repair hose damaged in blast!

definitions.meaning: to mend a hole in a stocking or sock by weaving thread across it
a mild exclamation of annoyance, like 'drat!'

explanation.surface: Someone curses a burst hosepipe that needs mending after an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' looks like a garden hosepipe, but it means stockings, the sense in which needlework repairs them.
explanation.definitionFit: Mending knitted socks with needle and wool is the classic sense; as an interjection the word is a softened curse.

clue.text: Layer of soil, perhaps, that's an addition to bank

definitions.meaning: matter laid down by a river or glacier, such as silt
money paid into a bank account

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from 'put down': sediment laid down naturally and money lodged with a bank.

clue.text: Criminal exhibited in gallery after being shot

definitions.text: Criminal exhibited in gallery after being shot

parts.words: Criminal exhibited in gallery after being shot
parts.note: read as a villain whose photograph is shown in a police collection of mugshots, shot meaning photographed

explanation.surface: A criminal is put on display after being gunned down.
explanation.walkthrough: A police 'gallery' of mugshots of known offenders is the picture; 'shot' means photographed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishonest scoundrel is a villain, whose photo appears in a police mugshot collection.

clue.text: Is upset over a small point

indicators.note: over signals that the word just found is turned round and read the other way

parts.note: a cart that tips is one that is upset, overturned

explanation.surface: Someone gets annoyed about a trivial detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns TIPS round. The surface reads as fuss about a minor matter, but the point is a geographical one: a narrow tongue of land jutting into water.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow projecting strip of sand or shingle running out into the sea is a modest headland.

clue.text: Digger down under

parts.note: read as a worker who digs below ground in a mine, not an Australian (a 'digger' Down Under)

explanation.definitionFit: A coal miner works at the bottom of a shaft, digging underground.

clue.text: Spare man on board, being rational

parts.note: spare means lean or thin
the king is a piece on a chessboard

explanation.surface: A substitute player sitting on a committee behaves sensibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' looks like a committee member; it is a chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who reasons and reflects is capable of reason.

clue.text: Competed on course with expert, in a way

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits within the letters of the other

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Someone ran a race on a track alongside a seasoned professional.
explanation.definitionFit: Contestants who ran against each other round a track took part in a contest of speed.

clue.text: Hood's purpose in robbery involving underworld boss in vengeance

indicators.note: involving means one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: retribution is vengeance
Dis is the Roman god of the underworld

explanation.surface: A gangster robs a bank as revenge on behalf of a crime lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' is Robin Hood, who robbed the rich to give to the poor, not a gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood stole from the rich to give to the poor, sharing wealth out differently.

clue.text: Having succeeded in hunt, shoot old gun

indicators.note: in tells us a letter goes inside the word for hunt

parts.note: a chase is a hunt
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies
to pot is to shoot

explanation.surface: After a successful hunt, someone fires an antique firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S inside CHASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A breech-loading rifle used by the French army in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Offered bait thus to fish in middle of eddy

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other
middle of takes the central letters of the word that follows

parts.note: to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: An angler hangs a lure into a whirlpool of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thus' points at the setter's own picture: a line dangled into the water to fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Held something tempting out to entice, as a hook hangs before a fish.

clue.text: He left daughter floundering to face financial difficulty

indicators.note: floundering suggests struggling confusion, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A father abandoned his daughter and now struggles to pay his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floundering' rearranges HE LEFT DAUGHTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being short of money, as if chilled by a cold current of air.

clue.text: Swineherds taking time in the shade

parts.note: men who tend pigs are pigmen

explanation.surface: Pig-keepers take a break resting out of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' looks like shelter from the sun; here it is a colour, as of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A colouring substance gives a particular hue, which is one sense of a shade.

clue.text: Inspired attraction in pub

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a draw is something that attracts crowds

explanation.surface: A popular feature at a local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspired' is used in its literal sense of breathed in, not creative.
explanation.definitionFit: Air drawn into the lungs is inhaled, the literal meaning of inspired.

clue.text: Old sailor taking light boat astern

parts.note: a shell is a light racing rowing boat
astern means at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: An elderly seaman tows a small rowing boat behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical slang for a veteran seaman, especially one who has crossed the equator.

clue.text: Material for rope in which girl's holding one back

indicators.note: back says the whole assembled piece is read in the reverse direction
holding means one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a lass is a girl; the 's stands for 'is'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rope-maker's fibre, in which a young woman is holding something back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts I inside LASS to give LASIS; 'back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough fibre from an agave plant, traditionally twisted into cord and twine.

clue.text: Skill rejected by cast as useless

indicators.note: rejected suggests the word is sent back, so read in reverse

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
to shy is to throw or cast

explanation.surface: An actor's talent is turned down by the cast as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ART into TRA. 'cast' looks like a theatre company but is a verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbishy, worthless stuff is of poor quality and no use.

clue.text: A lot of trees cut with assistance, as previously stated

indicators.note: cut means the final letter is chopped off

parts.note: a forest is a lot of trees
aid is assistance

explanation.surface: Lumberjacks felled many trees with help, as mentioned before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the last letter T of FOREST.
explanation.definitionFit: Already mentioned earlier in a document is the legalistic sense of this word.

clue.text: One group of conservationists taking perverse pride in being audacious

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation charity

indicators.note: perverse suggests something twisted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A conservationist takes stubborn pride in bold ventures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perverse' rearranges PRIDE into REPID.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a fearless, daring person who takes bold risks.

clue.text: Fish that quickly bite?

definitions.meaning: a family of warm-sea food fish
creatures that snap their jaws shut fast, the question mark flagging the whimsical sense

explanation.definitionFit: One name covers a family of tropical food fish and, literally, anything that bites with a snap.

clue.text: Triumphant about stick-in-the-mud finally pressing on

indicators.note: about means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: crowing is boasting in triumph

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A victor gloats over a dull conservative while carrying on regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes D, the last letter of 'stick-in-the-mud'; 'about' puts it inside CROWING.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing hard against people or things, as a crowd jostles forward, is to throng them.

clue.text: First form given chapter of great book, say

parts.note: class I is the first form in a school

explanation.surface: Young pupils are given a chapter of a famous novel to read.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a year group is a 'form'.
explanation.definitionFit: A work of lasting excellence, like a celebrated novel, is a masterpiece of literature.

clue.text: Relieved at being settled in retirement?

indicators.note: being settled in means a piece is lodged inside another

parts.note: abed means in bed, having retired for the night

explanation.surface: Someone feels relief at last having settled into their retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain that has lessened or subsided has been eased.

clue.text: Visionary measure protecting English monarch

indicators.note: protecting means one piece wraps around and shields the other

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of drink
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A far-sighted policy shields the English sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' puts E inside DRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist with lofty but impractical ideas sees visions.

clue.text: This may secure one's position by a fluke

definitions.text: This may secure one's position by a fluke

parts.words: This may secure one's position by a fluke
parts.note: read as a ship's heavy iron hook that holds a vessel in place by its fluke, the barbed blade that digs in, not by luck

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their job by pure luck.
explanation.walkthrough: A fluke is the flat pointed blade of a ship's mooring device.
explanation.definitionFit: A weighted hook dropped to the seabed holds a ship in place by its barbed arms.

clue.text: Scene of conflict as knight invades some land

indicators.note: invades means one piece enters the letters of another

parts.note: an area is a piece of land
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A medieval knight invades territory and a battle ensues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invades' puts N inside AREA.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where contests or fights take place, originally the sanded floor of a Roman amphitheatre.

clue.text: Go through exercises to secure grade

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
to net is to secure or catch
a rate is a grade or class, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A pupil gets through gym sessions in order to achieve a pass mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce or pass into something is to get through it.

clue.text: Collection of maps a sailor turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word reads upwards, in reverse

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman turns up with a book of charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses SALT to TLAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound book of maps is named after the Titan who held up the heavens.

clue.text: One reflects on a flamboyant costume

definitions.text: One reflects on a flamboyant costume

parts.words: One reflects on a flamboyant costume
parts.note: read as a sequin-like disc stitched on showy clothing that catches and reflects light, not a person reflecting

explanation.surface: Someone muses about an outrageous outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflects' suggests thinking; it means sending back light.
explanation.definitionFit: A small shiny disc sewn onto clothes for glitter flashes light back from a showy outfit.

clue.text: Crooked type of chimney cowl at the front

indicators.note: at the front means this piece comes before the other

parts.note: a cowl is a hood
lum is a Scottish and northern English word for chimney

explanation.surface: A description of a cowl fitted to the top of a chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' is used of a criminal, not a bent chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent small-time criminal or thug is a dishonest sort.

clue.text: Trainee policeman, perhaps, taking notes in court

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: A, D and E are musical notes

explanation.surface: A young officer writes things down during a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A young person training for the police or armed forces is a recruit; 'perhaps' marks the police as one example.

clue.text: Source of pain inflicted by scourge in odd places

indicators.note: in odd places picks the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Pain dealt out by a whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in odd places' takes S, O, R, E from 'scourge'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender, inflamed spot on the body hurts.

clue.text: Employer is one who offers guidance, not being hard-hearted

indicators.note: not being says the letter named next is dropped

parts.note: an usher guides people to their seats
H is the abbreviation for hard, here the middle letter

explanation.surface: A boss is a mentor who is kind rather than harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not being hard-hearted' removes H, the heart of USHER. 'Employer' means one who employs, i.e. makes use of something.
explanation.definitionFit: One who makes use of a thing employs it, so is literally an employer.
